title: Request: 请求补充 epoch_3.pt 的基因列表、运行环境和推理示例 / Request for reproducibility files for epoch_3.pt   Checkpoint-matched environment, attention semantics and minimal reference fixture
body:
各位作者好！

感谢开源 MAP 的代码和预训练权重。我想使用已发布的 epoch_3.pt 做推理评估，目前已完成权重文件和张量完整性检查，还没有运行模型前向计算。对照代码时，有几处细节不太确定，想请教一下：

1. 输出基因列表
能否提供解码器输出 0–1999 维对应的有序 2,000 个 HVG 列表？如果其中使用数字 ID，也请提供对应词表或映射方式。看到 Issue #3 已有类似提问，我也需要这份文件来解释输出。另外，想确认一下解码器预测值的归一化方法和表达尺度。

2. 配套代码和环境
能否告知与 epoch_3.pt 对应的源码版本和 Transformers 版本，以及是否修改过 LLaMA 的实现？

目前看到配置中 hidden_size=1024、num_attention_heads=8、head_dim=84，而检查点中的注意力投影权重是 1024×1024。不同 Transformers 版本对 _update_causal_mask 和 NoRoPE 的调用方式似乎也有差异。不确定是否是我遗漏了环境设置，想请您确认实际使用的 head dimension、因果或双向注意力、位置编码，以及 padding mask 和 attention backend 的设置。

3. 一个小型推理示例
如果方便，能否提供一份与该权重配套的示例输入和参考输出，以及预处理方式、随机种子和允许的数值误差？这样可以先核对推理结果，避免在环境适配时无意中改变模型行为。

4. 剂量设置
想确认输入剂量的单位、变换方式，以及发布的检查点是否实际使用了剂量条件。

这些问题与 Issue #3–#5 有部分关联。如果已有文件或说明，麻烦指一下链接即可，不需要另外整理完整数据集。如果暂时不方便提供全部材料，有序基因列表和配套环境信息就已经很有帮助。

后续使用 MAP 或您提供的材料开展研究并撰写论文时，我会引用 MAP 文献，并对相关帮助作适当致谢。

感谢各位老师的时间！


Dear MAP authors,

Thank you for sharing the MAP code and pretrained weights. I would like to evaluate the released epoch_3.pt without retraining. I have checked the weight files and tensor integrity, but have not yet run a forward pass. While reading the code, I came across a few details that I hope you could help clarify.

1. Output gene list
Could you share the ordered list of 2,000 HVGs corresponding to decoder output dimensions 0–1999? If these are numeric IDs, the matching vocabulary or mapping would also be helpful. I saw the related request in issue #3 and need the same file to interpret the outputs. Could you also confirm the normalization and expression scale of the decoder targets?

2. Matching code and environment
Which source revision and Transformers version should be used with epoch_3.pt? Were any local changes made to the LLaMA implementation?

The configuration I inspected specifies hidden_size=1024, num_attention_heads=8 and head_dim=84, while the checkpoint attention projection weights are 1024-by-1024. Transformers versions also appear to differ in how the _update_causal_mask and NoRoPE overrides are called. I may have missed an environment setting. Could you confirm the intended head dimension, causal or bidirectional attention, positional encoding, padding mask and attention backend?

3. A small inference example
If available, could you share a small example input and reference output for this checkpoint, along with the preprocessing, random seed and expected numerical tolerance? This would help check the inference results and avoid accidentally changing model behavior while adapting the environment.

4. Dose settings
Could you confirm the dose units and transformation, and whether the released checkpoint uses dose conditioning?

These questions partly overlap with issues #3–#5. Links to existing files or documentation would be sufficient; there is no need to prepare the full dataset. If only some materials are available, the ordered gene list and matching environment information would already be very helpful.

I will cite the MAP paper in any resulting manuscript that uses MAP or the materials you provide, and acknowledge your help appropriately.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

title: Request for missing pert_ca.py and bart_vocab.txt to reproduce MAP demo
body:
Dear Authors of the MAP paper,

I hope this email finds you well.

Thank you for releasing the code and pretrained weights for the MAP framework (Nature Machine Intelligence). 
When running demo.py, the following error occurs at the import stage:
text

from model.pert_ca import PerturbationEncoder_ca
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'model.pert_ca'

I have confirmed that model/pert_ca.py is not present in the public repository (commit b61d769, and also tried 4e16ce4), while model/pert.py exists. Several other related modules (such as certain dataset loaders) also appear to be missing.

More critically, model/mega_molbart/STMencoder_ddp.py requires bart_vocab.txt, which is also missing. This file cannot be substituted with any other BART vocabulary, because the checkpoint's smiles_encoder._model.emb.weight has shape (32000, 1024). The vocabulary size and token ordering must match training exactly.

Would it be possible for you to share:

    The missing pert_ca.py (or confirm that model/pert.py is the correct replacement), and

    The exact bart_vocab.txt used during training?

This would greatly help me and other users who wish to reproduce and apply the model. I have also posted this in GitHub Issue #5, where several users are blocked by the same problem.

Thank you very much for your time and for the valuable contribution of MAP to the field.

title: Several internal modules referenced by the repo are missing (`pert_ca.py` etc.), and two cluster paths are hard-coded
body:
Hi, and thanks for releasing the code and weights for MAP.

I've read the existing issues (#1–#4) and added my findings to them where they overlap. This is a separate problem, and it's the one that currently stops `demo.py` from starting at all.

**Summary:** a clean clone of `main` imports internal modules that aren't in the repository. `MAP/model/model.py` does `from model.pert_ca import PerturbationEncoder_ca` at module top level, so `demo.py`, `train.py` and `eval_tahoe.py` all fail during import — before any checkpoint, data or config is touched. I also found two hard-coded cluster paths in the MoleculeSTM loader.

I’d originally assumed the missing files were the whole story, but after getting `epoch_3.pt` I checked it against the code, and **most of the checkpoint is actually compatible** — details in the Update section near the end. So this may be a smaller fix than it first looked, but I still need your help on two specific items:

1. Is `PerturbationEncoder_ca` a genuinely different class, or did `model/pert_ca.py` just not get uploaded? (The checkpoint suggests the latter.)
2. Could you share `bart_vocab.txt`? It's needed by `MolSTM_Extractor` and cannot be substituted — the vocabulary size determines the embedding shape in the checkpoint.

I followed the README and verified my environment and all third-party dependencies, so this isn't a local setup problem.

Thanks!

---

## Environment (verified working — not the cause)

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (WSL2), kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 |
| Python | 3.10.20 (venv) |
| PyTorch | 2.12.0+cu130, `torch.cuda.is_available() == True` |
| GPU | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop, 8 GiB, cc8.9 |
| numpy / pandas / scipy | 2.2.6 / 2.3.3 / 1.15.3 |
| rdkit / omegaconf / safetensors | 2026.03.6 / 2.3.1 / 0.7.0 |
| scanpy / anndata / h5py | 1.11.5 / 0.11.4 / 3.16.0 |

Repository revision (fetched from `codeload.github.com`):

```
commit b61d7696f34c525b3035c499a6e83ed2ee1257d2
date   2026-07-02T02:08:40Z
subj   Create README.md
```

## Reproduction

```bash
cd MAP
python demo.py
```

## Exact error

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "demo.py", line 14, in <module>
    from model.model import MAPmodel
  File ".../MAP/model/model.py", line 8, in <module>
    from model.pert_ca import PerturbationEncoder_ca
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'model.pert_ca'
```

`MAP/model/pert_ca.py` is not present in the repository. This import is at module top level, so **every** script that reaches `model.model` fails immediately.

---

## Missing files

I located these by walking each entry point's local imports with itself as `sys.path` root. For each module, `X.py` (or `X/__init__.py`) is absent from the corresponding directory.

| # | Missing file | Imported as | Blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `MAP/model/pert_ca.py` | `from model.pert_ca import PerturbationEncoder_ca` | `MAP/demo.py`, `MAP/train.py`, `MAP/evaluate/eval_tahoe.py`, `MAP/evaluate/eval_multi_cell.py` — i.e. **the README's own demo and the main training/eval path** |
| 2 | `MAP/data/ds_nips_lora_se.py` | `from data.ds_nips_lora_se import NIPSPerturbDatasetSE` | `MAP/train_nips.py` (OP3) |
| 3 | `MAP/data/ds_sciplex_lora_se.py` | `from data.ds_sciplex_lora_se import SciplexPerturbDatasetSE` | `MAP/train_sciplex.py` (SciPlex3) |
| 4 | `MAP/data/ds_combosciplex_lora_se.py` | `from data.ds_combosciplex_lora_se import ComboSciplexPerturbDatasetSE` | `MAP/train_combosciplex.py`, `MAP/evaluate/eval_combosciplex.py`, `MAP/baseline_control.py`, `MAP/baseline_perturbmean.py` |
| 5 | `MAP/model/model_combosciplex_avg_emb.py` | `from model.model_combosciplex_avg_emb import MAPmodel` | `MAP/train_combosciplex.py`, `MAP/evaluate/eval_combosciplex.py` |
| 6 | `MAP/model/model_combosciplex_two_tokens.py` | `from model.model_combosciplex_two_tokens import MAPmodel` | `MAP/train_combosciplex.py`, `MAP/evaluate/eval_combosciplex.py` |

### File manifest evidence

`MAP/model/` currently contains exactly 8 files (plus the `mega_molbart/` package):

```
    5419  components.py
    4071  flash_transformer.py
    3658  gene_decoders.py
    5177  model.py
    4675  pert.py          <- note: pert.py exists, pert_ca.py does not
   15257  se.py
    2543  smiles_kg_encoder_v3.py
    7781  transformer_encoder.py
```

**1× `ds_multi_cell_lora_se.py` (Tahoe-100M)** is present, which is why `train.py` / `eval_tahoe.py` get as far as `model.model` and then fail on item #1. The pattern suggests `data/ds_*_lora_se.py` and `model/model_*.py` were added for each additional benchmark, but three dataset files and two model files did not make it into the public repo.

---

## Per-entry-point status

Method: for each script, parse its local imports (`data.*`, `model.*`, `evaluate.*`, `utils.*`, `configs.*`) and check for the file under that directory taken as the import root.

| Entry point | Status |
|---|---|
| `MAP/demo.py` | ❌ fails transitively via `model.model` → `model.pert_ca` |
| `MAP/train.py` | ❌ fails transitively via `model.model` → `model.pert_ca` |
| `MAP/evaluate/eval_tahoe.py` | ❌ fails transitively via `model.model` → `model.pert_ca` |
| `MAP/evaluate/eval_multi_cell.py` | ❌ fails transitively via `model.model` → `model.pert_ca` |
| `MAP/train_nips.py` | ❌ missing `data.ds_nips_lora_se` (and the above) |
| `MAP/train_sciplex.py` | ❌ missing `data.ds_sciplex_lora_se` (and the above) |
| `MAP/train_combosciplex.py` | ❌ missing 3 modules (and the above) |
| `MAP/evaluate/eval_combosciplex.py` | ❌ missing 3 modules (and the above) |
| `MAP/baseline_control.py` | ❌ missing `data.ds_combosciplex_lora_se` |
| `MAP/baseline_perturbmean.py` | ❌ missing `data.ds_combosciplex_lora_se` |
| `MAP-KG/train_resume.py` + `MAP-KG/data/dataload.py` + `MAP-KG/model/model.py` | ✅ all local imports resolve |
| `preprocess/A_` … `preprocess/G2_` (all 9 scripts) | ✅ all local imports resolve |

So **`MAP-KG/` and `preprocess/` are complete**, and the breakage is confined to `MAP/`.

---

## Update — what I found after obtaining `epoch_3.pt`

I've since got hold of the three Drive files, so I can report something more useful than the original request. **The news is mostly good.**

**(a) `all_embeddings` — resolved, no action needed.** `Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.gene_symbol_to_embedding_ESM2.pt` (410,886,729 bytes) is **byte-identical** to the `protein_embeddings.pt` shipped in `arcinstitute/SE-600M` — same SHA256 (`a210e1cc…7de9748`). So the Arc release can serve as `all_embeddings` for anyone who can't reach Drive. Thanks for pointing at it in #1.

**(b) The SE half of `epoch_3.pt` loads cleanly — you do not need to change anything there.** I diffed the checkpoint's `se.*` keys (239 tensors) against what the current code constructs:

```
code-constructed SE keys         : 238
key names matching checkpoint    : 238
same name but shape mismatch     : 0
only in checkpoint               : 1  → se.pe_embedding.weight
```

That single extra key is exactly the one `load_se_ckpt()` already lists in `expected_missing`. So no conversion or remapping is needed for the encoder.

**(c) `pert_ca.py` may not actually be needed — but I'd like your confirmation.** (This is the body of my report below.) Comparing the checkpoint's `pert_model.*` keys (260 tensors) against the components in the repo:

| checkpoint component | keys | present in `model/pert.py`? |
|---|---|---|
| `smiles_encoder._model.*` | 176 | ✅ `KGSmilesEncoder_v3.smiles_encoder` |
| `transformer_backbone.*` | 42 | ✅ LLaMA backbone |
| `cell_projector` / `gene_tokens_projector` / `drug_projector` / `project_out` / `gene_decoder` | 8 / 10 / 10 / 4 / 10 | ✅ all present |

That looks like `PerturbationEncoder` from `model/pert.py` (which `model.py` assigns to `self.pert_model`) rather than a distinct architecture. **So my question is: is `PerturbationEncoder_ca` actually a different class, or is the import in `model.py` just pointing at a module that didn't get uploaded?** If it's the latter, adding `pert_ca.py` (even a re-export) is the whole fix.

**(d) NEW — and this one I genuinely cannot work around.** `model/mega_molbart/STMencoder_ddp.py` hard-codes two cluster paths:

```python
ckpt_path  = "/mnt/petrelfs/fengjinghao/molecule_model.pth"
vocab_path = "/mnt/petrelfs/fengjinghao/CRAFT/VirtualCell/ours_v1/drug/MoleculeSTM/MoleculeSTM/bart_vocab.txt"
```

Instantiating `PerturbationEncoder` fails immediately on the missing `bart_vocab.txt`. **Could you share `bart_vocab.txt`?** It can't be substituted with another BART vocabulary, because `MolSTM_Extractor._load_model()` derives the embedding size from `len(self.tokenizer)` — and the checkpoint's `pert_model.smiles_encoder._model.emb.weight` is `(32000, 1024)`, so the vocabulary size and token ordering must match training exactly. (`molecule_model.pth` would also be useful for completeness, though the smiles-encoder weights do appear to be inside `epoch_3.pt` already.)

**(e) The 2000-gene HVG list is still open and affects 3 users.** #3 (plus the follow-up comments from @sadny-happy and @baijinming97) asks for the ordered `hvg_gene_ids` / `top2000_hvg_info_seurat_v3_batch_aware.pkl`. I hit the same wall: `preprocess/E_hvg_multi_celllines.py` uses unseeded `random.sample`, so the exact list and its order can't be regenerated. Without it, the `[B, S, 2000]` decoder output can't be mapped back to gene symbols. Please treat this as a **+1 on #3** rather than a new request.

**(f) One documentation nit that cost me some time.** `configs/se600m.yaml` says `nlayers: 8`, but `model/model.py` hard-codes `nlayers=16`, and `epoch_3.pt` is 16 layers. The YAML value is never used on that path, so it's misleading — worth correcting if convenient.

**(g) Also noted for #4's benefit:** the current `model/flash_transformer.py` uses a fused `qkv_proj`, matching your checkpoint. The `self_attn.in_proj_weight` mismatch reported in #4 only appears when `use_flash_attention` is false and the code falls back to PyTorch's stock `TransformerEncoderLayer`. With `use_flash_attention: True` (the shipped default) the SE keys line up.

---

## Minor observations (may be of interest)

1. **`MAP-KG` counts differ slightly from the paper.** Using `RainGate/MAP-KG` (`sha 2a9af1bd2645fef86fab495b85a1b08a52356e26`):

   | File | data rows | paper | delta |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `DRUG_merged_drugs_with_residuals.csv` | 187,989 | 187,089 drug nodes | +900 (+0.48%) |
   | `GENE_tahoe_filtered.csv` | 22,923 | 22,924 gene nodes | **−1** |
   | `DRUG-GENE_filtered_by_existing_drugs_and_genes.csv` | 420,364 | 428,192 drug–gene edges | −7,828 |
   | `GENE-GENE_filtered_by_existing_genes.csv` | 249,976 | 266,054 gene–gene edges | −16,078 |

   (Counting note: `GENE_tahoe_filtered.csv` has no trailing newline, so `wc -l` reports 22,922 — it actually holds 22,924 lines = 1 header + 22,923 records, i.e. one short of the paper's 22,924.)

   Total edges: **670,340 vs 694,246 in the paper (−3.44%)**. Node counts are within 0.5%, but the edge deficit is larger. Likely a version drift between the Hub release and the submitted version — flagging in case it's unintended.

2. **`smile_encoder` default differs across entry points.** `MAP/train.py` defaults to `MAP-KG`, while `MAP/evaluate/eval_tahoe.py` defaults to `PrimeKG_ver1` and `MAP/demo.py` hard-codes `"PrimeKG_ver1"` (line 80). I assume this is intentional for the knowledge-scaling ablation, but it means the demo loads a different drug encoder than the main training script unless the checkpoint matches — worth a note in the README.

3. **`control_indices` naming mismatch.** `preprocess/Cs_split_unseen_combination.py` writes `control_indices_UC.json`, while `MAP/demo.py` reads `control_indices.json` (no `_UC`). Easy to hit when following the README end-to-end. (I worked around it with a copy.)

4. **`MAP-KG/data/selected_csvs/` vs `data/selected_data_csvs/`.** The README says to place the MAP-KG CSVs under `MAP-KG/data/selected_csvs/`, but `MAP-KG/train_resume.py`'s `TrainingConfig` reads from `data/selected_data_csvs/`.

5. **DEG significance test.** The Methods section describes a Wilcoxon rank-sum test with FDR control, while `MAP/evaluate/eval_utils.py::get_significant_deg_mask` uses `scipy.stats.ttest_ind(..., equal_var=False)` with an uncorrected p-value threshold (and falls back to a global `|Δ|` ranking when fewer than `de_topk` genes are significant). This makes the top-50 DEG metrics not directly comparable to the paper. If a Wilcoxon + BH variant is what generated the reported numbers, it might be worth aligning the released code.

---

## Happy to help

If it's easier, I'm glad to test any of the missing files as soon as they're available, or to share the full import-resolution script I used to produce the table above. Thanks again for the release.

<sub>Details of the checks above, including the per-entry-point import resolution output, are available on request.</sub>

title: Request for matching pretrained weights for current demo.py / model code
body:
Hi, thank you for releasing MAP!

I am trying to run the official demo with the current code from this repository, but encounter severe `state_dict` mismatch when loading the checkpoint.

**Environment:**
- Code: latest from https://github.com/MAGIC-AI4Med/MAP
- Checkpoint: `epoch_3.pt` (downloaded from the Google Drive link in the README)
- Also tried the code from commit `4e16ce4` (May 7, 2026), but the mismatch persists.
- Command:
```bash
python demo.py \
  --ckpt ./epoch_3.pt \
  --cell_line CVCL_0023 \
  --drug_smiles "CC1=NC=C(C(=C1O)CO" \
  --drug_conc 0.5 \
  --output_dir ./demo_output \
  --se_config ./configs/se600m.yaml \
  --se_ckpt ./se600m.safetensors
Error (abbreviated):
textRuntimeError: Error(s) in loading state_dict for MAPmodel:
    Missing key(s) in state_dict: 
        "se.transformer_encoder.layers.0.self_attn.in_proj_weight",
        "se.transformer_encoder.layers.0.self_attn.in_proj_bias",
        ...
    Unexpected key(s) in state_dict: 
        "se.transformer_encoder.layers.0.qkv_proj.weight",
        "se.transformer_encoder.layers.0.qkv_proj.bias",
        ...
Key observations:

Transformer naming mismatch:
Current code expects the older-style keys: self_attn.in_proj_weight / out_proj
The checkpoint contains the newer/custom style: qkv_proj / out_proj

Perturbation encoder structure mismatch:
Current code expects keys under pert_model.kg_smiles_encoder.smiles_encoder...
The checkpoint has keys under pert_model.smiles_encoder... (without the kg_ prefix)


Request:
Could you please provide:

The exact commit (or a specific tag/branch) that is fully compatible with epoch_3.pt.
The recommended way to load both the main checkpoint and the SE weights (se600m.safetensors).
Any additional files that are required for the official demo to run successfully.

Thank you very much for your help!

title: Request: shared_hvg/hvg_info (the 2000-HVG gene list) needed to interpret the released decoder outputs
body:
Thank you for releasing MAP's code and pretrained weights!

When running inference with the released `epoch_3.pt`, the predicted `pred_hvgs` are [B, S, 2000] vectors whose 2000 output positions are positionally tied to the shared HVG gene list computed by `preprocess/E_hvg_multi_celllines.py` (batch-aware seurat_v3, 8 cell lines, 10k cells/line). The list itself (the `shared_hvg/hvg_info` / `hvg_gene_ids` artifact) does not appear to be included in the Google Drive weights folder or the RainGate/MAP-KG HuggingFace dataset, and because the selection involves unseeded sampling (`random.sample`), it cannot be reproduced exactly from the script.

Without the exact list (and its order), the released decoder's gene-level outputs cannot be mapped to gene symbols, which blocks any gene-level evaluation with the released checkpoint (e.g., top-50 DEG Pearson delta correlation against an external panel, or GSEA).

Would it be possible to share the `hvg_gene_ids` list (the order matters) — e.g., added to the Google Drive folder or the HF dataset? Alternatively, the per-cell-line split JSONs (`{cell_line}_indices.json`) would also be very helpful for reproducing the paper's evaluation protocol.

Thanks again — the framework is a great contribution to the perturbation-prediction field.

title: Request: Demo sample data & checkpoint file mapping
body:
Hi, thanks for the great work! I'd like to run the demo but have two quick questions:

1. Could you provide a minimal preprocessed data sample for CVCL_0023 so we don't need to download the full Tahoe-100M (~4TB) just to test demo.py?
2. The Google Drive folder has three .pt files — could you briefly clarify which file corresponds to which model component (--ckpt, --se_ckpt, Cell-stateFoundation Model,  Molecule Encoder etc.)?

A short note in the README would be super helpful. Thanks.

title: Request for missing file Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.gene_symbol_to_embedding_ESM2.pt
body:
Hello @Raingate,

Thank you for sharing your work on MAP. I am trying to reproduce the knowledge encoder pre-training, but the script D_extract_se_emb.py (and later train_resume.py) fails because it cannot find the file Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.gene_symbol_to_embedding_ESM2.pt. This file is referenced in configs/se600m.yaml and model/model.py.

I have already downloaded the CSV data from Hugging Face, but this .pt file is not included. Could you please provide a download link for this file (or clarify how to generate it)? It would be very helpful for the community to fully replicate your results. Thank you!
